WETA × NAVIER
The Bay runs on water.
Navier makes it fly.

A right-sized electric ferry layer for service WETA operates today—and waterfront links it could test next.

Built in Alameda. Designed for the Bay.
Partner discussion draft · Passenger service first · July 2026
Sources: WETA 2050 Service Vision · Navier N30 platform

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
A right-sized electric layer for the Bay
LOWER COST TO SERVE
Hydrofoiling and electric propulsion reduce energy demand and remove marine-fuel exposure.
MORE SERVICE OPTIONS
Add frequency, start smaller, or test a waterfront link before committing to large-ferry scale.
BETTER PASSENGER EXPERIENCE
Designed for a quieter, smoother, lower-wake ride—validated in Bay trials.
LOCAL DELIVERY PARTNER
Navier is based in Alameda, close to WETA’s network, terminals and operating environment.
Sources: WETA 2050 Service Vision · WETA REEF · Navier N30 platform

THE MANDATE
WETA is building the Bay’s next ferry network

TODAY
A nine-terminal public network is moving toward zero-emission service.

NEXT
Mission Bay, Treasure Island, Berkeley and Redwood City are in WETA’s published expansion program.

THE OPENING
Use a smaller electric hydrofoil where WETA needs more frequency, a lower-risk market start, or an underserved waterfront link.
Sources: WETA 2050 Service Vision · WETA REEF and expansion project pages

INTRODUCING THE N30
A small electric ferry that flies above the chop
RANGE
70+ nautical miles at 20 knots.
SPEED
20-knot cruise. 30-knot top speed.
CHARGING
DC fast charging in approximately 45 minutes.
RIDE CONTROL
Active flight control adjusts up to 50 times per second.
HOW IT WORKS
Hydrofoils lift the hull above the waves. Electric propulsion moves it quietly. Active flight control continually adjusts the ride. Public-service configuration and operating limits require WETA and regulatory validation.
Source: Navier N30 platform specifications

WHY THE COST TO SERVE CAN FALL
Hydrofoiling changes the energy equation

UP TO 90% LOWER ENERGY USE* · The hull flies above the chop, reducing drag.
ELECTRIC POWER · No marine-fuel exposure and fewer combustion-engine systems.
RIGHT-SIZED SERVICE · Add trips and capacity in smaller increments.
SOFTWARE PATH · Remote monitoring now; autonomy only after certification and WETA approval.

*Navier company estimate; route-specific energy use and lifecycle economics require Bay validation.
Sources: Navier N30 platform · Navier company and autonomy materials

THE PASSENGER EXPERIENCE
Silent. Smooth. Designed for public service.
A CALMER RIDE
Active flight control responds to chop while the hull travels above much of the wave action.
A BETTER CABIN
Quiet electric propulsion, no exhaust fumes and wide views support a comfortable, conversational trip.
PUBLIC TRANSIT BY DESIGN
Accessibility, boarding, bikes, luggage, fare integration and cabin layout must be designed with WETA.
Sources: Navier N30 platform · SF Bay Ferry passenger and accessibility standards

CONFIDENCE
Built in Alameda. Ready to learn on the Bay.
The N30 is a current platform for validating the hydrofoil stack, charging, Bay operating data and passenger experience before public-service decisions.
START WITH WHAT EXISTS
Use the N30 to test the vessel, energy system and operating evidence now.
EXPAND ONLY WITH PROOF
Larger foiling platforms and autonomy remain future pathways—not requirements or commitments.
Sources: Navier N30 platform · Navier company and autonomy materials

HOW IT WORKS
One network, three roles for right-sized vessels
STRENGTHEN EXISTING SERVICE
Add targeted frequency or a smaller capacity increment where WETA identifies a real rider need.
LAUNCH PUBLISHED EXPANSION
Give an emerging market a practical electric starting point while WETA learns demand and operations.
OPEN OVERLOOKED LINKS
Test a waterfront-to-waterfront trip where road travel is indirect and large-ferry demand is not yet proven.
START SMALL
Begin with one bounded public problem and a clear operating hypothesis.
GROW WITH DATA
Add frequency, vessels or capacity only after real Bay performance is known.
WETA DECIDES
WETA retains network, safety, procurement and public-service authority.
Source: WETA 2050 Service Vision and Expansion Policy

Sources: Navier Bay network render · WETA REEF and expansion project pages

STEP 1
Run a WETA-shaped Bay demonstration from Alameda

Before choosing a public route, test the N30 against WETA’s operating questions.

• Safety case and operating envelope
• Energy use, charging and range reserve
• Reliability, maintenance and crew workflow
• Ride quality, wake and noise
• Terminal interface and emergency procedures

OUTPUT · A shared evidence pack—not a route or procurement commitment.
Sources: WETA pilot framework · Navier Alameda and N30 materials

STEP 2
Pilot one WETA-selected public-service use case
ONE USE CASE
After certification, accessibility, terminal, charging, labor and procurement requirements are satisfied, pilot one WETA-selected use case.
MEASURE WHAT MATTERS
Energy and cost per trip · availability · on-time performance · maintenance · rider experience · accessibility · operator and community feedback.
DECIDE BEFORE SCALING
Agree success and stop thresholds before launch. WETA decides whether to continue, modify or stop.
Sources: WETA 2050 pilot framework · SF Bay Ferry public-service standards

STEP 3
Scale only when the evidence supports it

1 · Add frequency or vessels on a successful pilot.
2 · Extend to another WETA-selected market.
3 · Introduce larger-capacity foiling vessels when ready.
4 · Add autonomy only after safety, certification and operating proof.

Each step follows WETA approval, procurement, terminal, labor and community processes.
Partner discussion draft · Passenger service first · Subject to WETA and regulatory review
Sources: WETA 2050 Service Vision · Navier platform and autonomy materials

Sources: WETA 2050 Service Vision · SF Bay Ferry standards · Navier N30 platform
DELIVERY GATES
Six questions to answer before passenger service

SAFETY + CERTIFICATION · Is the USCG pathway and operating envelope clear?
ACCESSIBLE PUBLIC SERVICE · Can boarding, seating, bikes, luggage and fare integration work?
TERMINAL + CHARGING · Are berth access, shore power and turnaround practical?
BAY OPERATING FIT · Do weather, sea state, range reserve, wake and navigation meet requirements?
CREW + MAINTENANCE · Can WETA train, staff, maintain and dispatch the service reliably?
ECONOMICS + PUBLIC VALUE · Does lifecycle cost improve useful access and rider outcomes?
